newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Thousands of Jamaicans mourn Manley's death.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Jamaicans mourn Manley's death.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Jamaicans paced through the National Arena early on Friday to pay their respects to former Prime Minister Michael Manley, who died on March 6.

The opening procession for public viewing of Manley's body on Friday morning was led by Prime Minister P.J. Patterson, cabinet ministers, other politicians, schoolchildren, nurses in uniform, athletes and a street-cleaning crew.

By noon, a line snaked for hundreds of yards outside the arena, as mourners, many dressed in their Sunday best, waited patiently for a chance to see their hero one last time. A small group from Manley's People's National Party held a banner reading, "Michael Manley -- champion of the poor."
Police estimated more than 20,000 people had filed past the flag-draped, open wooden coffin.
Manley's coffin was surrounded by plants and flowers, and the walls of the arena were draped in black, gold and green bunting.
Songs by a children's choir alternated with solemn classical music. The Jamaica defence and police forces mounted an honour guard.

Manley died at home, aged 72, after a long struggle with cancer. Tributes came from labourers, communists and monarchs in honour of a man considered a father of Caribbean independence and a champion of working people and Third World rights.
Britain's Queen Elizabeth expressed her condolences to Manley's family, and Cuban President Fidel Castro mourned the loss of a "personal friend."

A state funeral was scheduled for Sunday afternoon, and Manley was to be interred at National Heroes Circle, next to former prime minister Sir Donald Sangster, a distant relative, and near his father Norman, his mother Edna, and his cousin former prime minister Sir Alexander Bustamante.

Jamaican officials have not released a list of dignitaries expected to attend the funeral, citing security concerns. Those expected to come included Castro, former U.S. President Jimmy Carter and former Canadian prime minister Pierre Trudeau.
